plain.text: This is the beginning of the good news about Jesus, the Christ, the Son of God. Long before, the prophet Isaiah said God would send a messenger to get people ready. That messenger was John the Baptist. He lived in the desert, wore clothes made of camel hair and ate locusts and wild honey. Crowds came to him. They confessed their sins and he baptised them in the Jordan River. John said, "Someone greater than me is coming. I baptise with water, but he will baptise you with the Holy Spirit."

Jesus came from Nazareth and was baptised by John. As he came up out of the water, he saw heaven torn open and the Spirit coming down on him like a dove. A voice from heaven said, "You are my Son, whom I love. I am pleased with you." Straight away the Spirit sent Jesus into the desert. He stayed there forty days and was tempted by Satan. Wild animals were there, and angels looked after him.

After John was put in prison, Jesus went to Galilee. He announced God's good news: "The time has come. God's kingdom is near. Turn back to God and believe the good news!" Walking by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two fishermen, Simon and Andrew. "Follow me," he said, "and I will make you fishers of people." They left their nets and followed him. Then he called James and John, who left their father in the boat and went with him.

In the town of Capernaum, Jesus taught in the synagogue on the Sabbath. People were amazed, because he taught with real authority, not like the religious teachers. A man with an evil spirit cried out, "I know who you are, the Holy One of God!" Jesus told the spirit to be quiet and come out, and it did. Everyone was astonished, and news about Jesus spread quickly.

Jesus went to the home of Simon and Andrew. Simon's mother-in-law was in bed with a fever. Jesus took her hand and helped her up, and the fever left her. That evening the whole town gathered at the door. Jesus healed many sick people and drove out many demons.

Very early, while it was still dark, Jesus went to a quiet place to pray. Simon and the others went looking for him and said, "Everyone is looking for you!" Jesus answered, "Let's go to other towns so I can preach there too. That is why I came." So he travelled around Galilee, preaching and driving out demons.

A man with a skin disease called leprosy knelt in front of Jesus and begged, "If you are willing, you can make me clean." Jesus felt deep compassion. He reached out, touched the man and said, "I am willing. Be clean!" The disease left him at once. Jesus told him not to tell anyone, but to show himself to the priest. Instead, the man told everyone. After that, Jesus could not openly enter a town, but people still came to him from everywhere.

summary.bigIdea: Jesus arrives with God's authority, announcing that God's kingdom is near and calling people to follow him.
points: John the Baptist prepares the way, and God calls Jesus his beloved Son at his baptism.
Jesus calls ordinary fishermen to follow him, and they leave everything.
Jesus teaches with authority, heals the sick, drives out evil spirits and makes time to pray.
summary.reflection: Jesus said, "Follow me." What would it look like for you to take one step of following him this week?
